- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.22) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope after peak.
- If model forecast mean is consistently below true outcome over 3–5 days, suggest mean reversion bias — increase forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence with observed trend.
- When sentiment is positive and price is falling, model often underestimates the fall; increase forecast decline rate by 10–20% to match sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period price recovery; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive or neutral.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.22 at 2–3 consecutive days), model tends to ignore sentiment and forecast flat — force a slight downward bias to reflect risk aversion.
